skills.name: repo-scout
skills.description: Map an unfamiliar codebase before changing it. Use when joining a repository, debugging an unclear subsystem, or planning work that depends on understanding project structure.

skills.name: spec-first
skills.description: Turn a feature request into testable acceptance criteria and a small implementation plan before editing. Use when requirements are ambiguous, a task spans several files, or a change may affect existing behavior.

skills.name: test-driven-change
skills.description: Implement a behavior change with tests that demonstrate the requirement and protect regressions. Use for bug fixes, new features, and changes with observable inputs and outputs.

skills.name: failure-forensics
skills.description: Diagnose a reproducible software failure by narrowing symptoms to a root cause and verifying the repair. Use for crashes, incorrect results, flaky tests, and hard-to-explain regressions.

skills.name: review-lens
skills.description: Review a diff for actionable correctness, security, reliability, and maintainability defects. Use before merging a change or when asked for an independent code review.

skills.name: security-surface
skills.description: Perform a focused threat review of code, APIs, configuration, and dependencies. Use when a change touches authentication, authorization, uploads, external input, secrets, payments, or sensitive data.

skills.name: dependency-care
skills.description: Evaluate dependency updates and vulnerabilities without creating avoidable breakage. Use when upgrading packages, responding to advisories, or cleaning dependency drift.

skills.name: performance-proof
skills.description: Find and validate a measurable performance bottleneck before optimizing. Use when latency, throughput, memory use, render speed, or compute cost is a concern.

skills.name: api-contract-check
skills.description: Check API and schema changes for compatibility with existing clients and stored data. Use when editing public endpoints, CLI flags, event payloads, database schemas, or serialized formats.

skills.name: docs-sync
skills.description: Bring documentation, examples, and configuration guides into agreement with the actual code. Use after behavior changes or when instructions may have drifted.

skills.name: data-quality-gate
skills.description: Design validation checks for structured datasets and data pipelines. Use when ingesting, transforming, joining, exporting, or versioning data used by software or machine-learning systems.

skills.name: dataset-workshop
skills.description: Prepare consistent, traceable instruction-tuning or evaluation datasets with reproducible cleaning rules. Use for JSONL corpora, reasoning examples, SFT data, or team-based dataset contributions.

skills.name: experiment-ledger
skills.description: Make ML training experiments reproducible and comparable. Use when fine-tuning models, comparing hyperparameters, changing datasets, or sharing GPU resources across contributors.

skills.name: model-eval-design
skills.description: Build an evaluation plan that measures a model capability rather than a single attractive example. Use when comparing base and fine-tuned models, reasoning systems, prompts, or agent workflows.

skills.name: model-diff-review
skills.description: Compare two model checkpoints or prompt configurations using a consistent evaluation harness and error taxonomy. Use after fine-tuning, quantization, prompt edits, or inference-stack changes.

skills.name: safe-migration
skills.description: Plan and execute a controlled migration of code, schemas, frameworks, or configuration while preserving a rollback path. Use when changing formats, APIs, databases, runtimes, or major dependencies.

skills.name: build-rescue
skills.description: Investigate and repair a failing build or CI job from logs to a verified fix. Use when compilers, linters, tests, containers, or CI workflows break.

skills.name: release-readiness
skills.description: Assess whether a change is ready for a tagged release or deployment. Use before publishing a package, shipping a production build, or announcing a new version.

skills.name: context-handoff
skills.description: Create a reliable handoff note so another engineer or coding agent can continue work without redoing exploration. Use before switching sessions, handing off a long task, or pausing midway.

skills.name: multi-agent-crosscheck
skills.description: Use independent reviewers or model providers to challenge a plan or diff and synthesize evidence-based disagreement. Use for high-impact, ambiguous, or research-heavy decisions when multiple agents are actually available.

skills.name: change-narrative
skills.description: Write a useful pull request or change summary that leads with the problem, impact, and proof. Use when preparing a handoff, code review request, release note, or engineering change record.

skills.name: parallel-task-design
skills.description: Break a multi-part engineering task into safely parallel work units with clear ownership and integration points. Use when several agents or contributors can work concurrently.

skills.name: sql-integrity-check
skills.description: Review SQL queries and data-model changes for correctness, access scope, safe parameterization, and performance. Use when writing joins, filters, migrations, reports, or analytics queries.

skills.name: research-evidence-map
skills.description: Turn a technical research question into a traceable evidence map with source quality, uncertainty, and actionable next experiments. Use for model architecture choices, benchmark claims, library selection, and unfamiliar technical topics.

skills.name: agent-skill-audit
skills.description: Validate a skill library for metadata correctness, discoverability, duplicate naming, risky instructions, and portability. Use when adding, reviewing, packaging, or publishing agent skills.
